description: We’re a group of students interested in engineering, space, and technology. We enjoy exploring new ideas, solving problems, and learning through hands-on projects. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we hope to combine our skills in engineering and coding to develop a creative and practical solution to the challenge we choose.
summary:
Abandoned but not forgotten is an interactive 3D storytelling experience about the machines NASA has left behind on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Visitors travel through four scenes: Apollo-era hardware on the Moon, the Mars rovers (including Opportunity’s final days during the 2018 global dust storm), Voyager 1 at the edge of the solar system, and a finale where hardware from every mission comes together.
Nine glowing hotspots reveal the story behind each machine, and short animated films with cited sources let curious visitors learn more. Sound effects and drag-to-look and zoom controls make it feel like being there. At the end, each visitor writes a short message to the next explorer, which is launched into space as fireworks.
We built it to answer the challenge by turning “discarded equipment” into something people care about. These machines are not junk, they are humanity’s footprints on other worlds. It runs in any browser as a single page with no install, so anyone can explore it on a phone or laptop.
details:
What it does
Abandoned but not Forgotten is an interactive 3D story about the machines NASA has left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Visitors move through four scenes: lunar hardware, the Mars rovers, Voyager 1, and a finale. They drag to look around, scroll to zoom, and tap glowing hotspots to unlock the story of each machine. Nine discoveries are hidden across the scenes, and short animated films with cited sources go deeper. In the finale, each visitor writes a message to the next explorer, which is launched into space as fireworks.

Why it matters / intended impact
Discarded equipment is easy to see as junk. We wanted people to see it as humanity’s footprints on other worlds, with real stories: Opportunity outlasted its planned mission by about 55 times before a global dust storm silenced it in 2018, and Voyager 1 is still travelling. The project turns facts into something people feel, so students and the public connect with the history of space exploration.

Tools and technology
It’s a single web page built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The 3D scenes use Three.js, and the machines are modelled in code rather than imported files. The films are drawn with the Canvas API, and all sound effects are generated live with the Web Audio API. It’s hosted on GitHub Pages, so it runs in any modern browser with no install.

Creativity
We combined exploration, storytelling, animation and sound in one experience, and ended it with a personal moment where visitors leave a message of their own.

Factors we considered
Accuracy (sources are cited in each film), accessibility (keyboard support, screen-reader announcements, reduced-motion support, larger touch targets) and ease of access on both phones and computers.
